what_happened: The operator accepted the design for the cutover job (20261025-001232-vesh) without working out what the required history check does on a pull request's head after the cutover point C0. The check judges the pull request's own unmerged commits by the attribution rule, so every pull request fails the full history check (PR #175). The cutover's tests only ran on histories shaped like main, not on a pull request branch.
cause: Plan review has no required realistic fixture for changes to a required check that walks commit ranges. Plans are judged and tested against main-shaped or job-only histories. Nothing makes the planner or reviewer run the check on a pull request branch shaped like this repository's, which has unmerged commits, operator commits, records-only commits and interventions. A rule that is correct on main therefore fails every pull request when it is applied to the pull request head.
prevention: Add a required test, and a plan-review gate, for any job that changes a required history or landing check. The test builds a fixture by running the real writers. It must contain a pull request branch with unmerged job commits, operator commits, records-only commits and declared interventions, both before and after the cutover point. The check must pass on that fixture, and the plan cannot be accepted until the gate shows it passing. A check that judges a pull request head must have a test case for that head.
proposed_request: Fix the required full history check so that it passes on a pull request whose head is after the cutover point C0 (see PR #175). Outcome: the check applies the attribution rule only to commits that have landed on main after C0. A pull request's own unmerged commits are not judged by that rule. A pull request that is shaped like this repository's gets a pass, including one with job commits, operator commits, records-only commits and declared interventions. Acceptance: (1) a test builds a branch history using the real writers, with main after C0 and a pull request branch carrying those commit kinds, and the check passes on it; (2) the same fixture with a real attribution violation on main after C0 still fails the check; (3) the empty case (a pull request with no commits beyond base) passes; (4) the existing cutover tests still pass. Do not rely on commit-message trailers. Afterwards, PR #175 and later pull requests can pass the check without operator intervention.
